label: The counterparty is a micro or small enterprise
definition: A supplier registered under the MSMED Act as a micro or small enterprise, whose invoices attract a statutory maximum payment period, statutory compound interest on delay that cannot be contracted away, and deferral of the buyer's income-tax deduction until payment is actually made.

authority.act: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006
authority.note: Payment by the agreed date or 45 days from the day of acceptance, whichever is earlier. Where no date is agreed, 15 days. An agreement fixing a longer period is void to that extent.

authority.act: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006
authority.note: Compound interest with monthly rests at three times the RBI notified bank rate. Not contractible away.

The buyer's deduction is deferred until the sum is actually paid. Applies to MICRO AND SMALL ONLY, not medium. Traders are excluded: wholesale and retail traders were admitted to MSME classification in 2021 for priority-sector lending only, and the delayed-payment protections were not extended to them.

enterprise_class.note: Medium is deliberately absent. s.43B(h) does not reach medium enterprises.

registered_on_supply_date.note: Registration must exist on the DATE OF SUPPLY, not merely today.

agreed_payment_days.note: Read from intake so the builder can detect a period longer than 45 days and clamp it.

a_structured.note: FIELD DOES NOT EXIST YET. The intake has no MSME or Udyam question anywhere in its 244 fields. This concept cannot resolve until it is added.

d_classifier.note: Deliberately disabled. A buyer's counterparty's Udyam status is not discoverable from any free text in the intake, and inferring it from a company name would be a fabrication with a tax consequence. This concept is declared or it is nothing.

confirmation.question: Is the supplier registered on Udyam as a micro or small enterprise?
confirmation.why: If it is, the law caps your payment period at 45 days, fixes the interest rate on any delay, and denies you the income-tax deduction until you have actually paid.

unresolved_behaviour.safe_default_note: Draft the 45-day version. A shorter payment period is always lawful, so assuming the cap is the safe direction; assuming its absence is not.
unresolved_behaviour.rationale: The buyer frequently does not know the supplier's Udyam status, so 'I don't know' is a common and legitimate answer rather than an edge case. Drafting 90 days silently would be the failure mode this design exists to prevent.

authoring_note: Chosen as the worked example in the specification because it looks like a boolean and is not: four qualifications (micro/small only, traders excluded, registration must exist on the supply date, day-of-acceptance runs from delivery unless objected to within 15 days) each break a flat flag.
